reconcile.note: Clarke reads the lion's Genesis 9:2 dread as territorial avoidance of human dwellings rather than submission or retreat in a direct encounter.

discrepancy.emptyNote: EvilBible.com's Christopher A. Baba sets Genesis's universal grant of animal dread against Proverbs's fearless lion that turns away from no one.

sides.snippet: The fear of you and the dread of you will be on every animal of the earth, and on every bird of the sky.
sides.verseText: The fear of you and the dread of you will be on every animal of the earth, and on every bird of the sky. Everything that the ground teems with, and all the fish of the sea are delivered into your hand.

sides.snippet: The lion, which is mightiest among animals, And doesn't turn away for any;
sides.verseText: The lion, which is mightiest among animals, And doesn't turn away for any;
